title: 13. Networking Basics
content:
# 13. Networking Basics

Troubleshoot connection issues, check open ports, and manage network interfaces.

## The Request Flow

How `curl google.com` actually works:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Shell
    participant DNS
    participant Server
    
    User->>Shell: curl google.com
    Shell->>DNS: Where is google.com?
    DNS-->>Shell: 142.250.xxx.xxx
    Shell->>Server: HTTP GET / (to IP)
    Server-->>Shell: 200 OK (HTML)
    Shell-->>User: Display HTML
```

## Diagnostics

-   **`ping <host>`**: The "Hello World" of networking. Checks connectivity using ICMP.
    ```bash
    ping google.com
    # Press Ctrl+C to stop!
    ```
-   **`ip a`** (or `ifconfig`): Show my IP addresses and interfaces.
    -   `lo`: Loopback (127.0.0.1). Talking to yourself.
    -   `eth0` / `enp3s0`: Wired Ethernet.
    -   `wlan0`: Wi-Fi.
-   **`netstat`** or **`ss`**: Who is listening?
    ```bash
    # Show Listening Ports (TCP & UDP) with numeric values
    ss -tuln
    ```

## DNS (Domain Name System)

Translate "google.com" (human friendly) to "142.250.xxx.xxx" (computer friendly).

-   **`nslookup google.com`**: Simple query.
-   **`dig google.com`**: Detailed query. Shows the exact DNS server used and query time.

## File Transfer / HTTP

-   **`curl`**: Client URL. The swiss-army knife of HTTP.
    ```bash
    curl https://api.github.com/users/defunkt
    curl -I google.com  # Fetch headers only (Debug 404s/500s)
    curl -O https://example.com/file.zip  # Download file
    ```
-   **`wget`**: Great for downloading large files or mirroring websites. Resumes broken downloads better than curl.
    ```bash
    wget -c https://example.com/movie.mp4
    ```

## Deep Dive: Localhost
`localhost` or `127.0.0.1` is **this computer**. If you run a web server on port 3000, you access it at `http://localhost:3000`. No traffic leaves your machine.

## Pro Tip: My Public IP
`ip a` shows your *local* network IP (e.g., 192.168.1.50). To see how the internet sees you:
```bash
curl ifconfig.me
```

## Practice Challenge
1.  Ping `8.8.8.8` (Google DNS).
2.  Use `curl` to fetch your own public IP.
3.  Check which ports are open on your machine with `ss -tuln`.
